steps.title: Four patterns for reading A1 Arabic
body: You have read real Arabic words and short sentences since the start. This lesson names four of the patterns behind them, so you can read new sentences with confidence: how nouns count, how "a" and "the" work, how a sentence can have no verb, and how to say "not".
Every example here uses words you already know.

steps.title: One, two, or many
body: A noun is singular, dual (exactly two), or plural.
The dual just adds ـَانِ: كِتَابٌ (a book) → كِتَابَانِ (two books).
Plurals are either regular — ـُونَ for groups of people, ـَاتٌ for many feminine things — or "broken", reshaped inside the word: كِتَابٌ → كُتُبٌ. You learn broken plurals one at a time.
A plural of non-human things counts as feminine singular for its adjective: كُتُبٌ جَمِيلَةٌ.

steps.title: "a" and "the"
body: An indefinite noun ("a book") ends in tanwīn — a doubled vowel, usually ـٌ, pronounced "-un": كِتَابٌ.
A definite noun ("the book") takes الـ at the front and drops the tanwīn: الْكِتَابُ.
A noun never carries الـ and tanwīn at the same time.

steps.title: A sentence with no verb
body: Arabic has no present-tense word for "is" or "are". A sentence can be just a definite noun followed by an indefinite describing word:
الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ — literally "the-house big" — means "The house is big."
If you make the second word definite too (الْبَيْتُ الْكَبِيرُ) it is no longer a sentence — it just means "the big house".

steps.title: Saying "not"
body: To negate this kind of sentence, put لَيْسَ ("is not") in front — and the describing word then takes ـً:
لَيْسَ الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرًا — "The house is not big."
لَا before a noun means "no …" / "there is no …": لَا مَاءَ (no water).

steps.title: Read them aloud
steps.intro: Twelve short sentences using these four patterns. Tap 🔊 to hear each one, then reveal the meaning to check yourself.

steps.title: Quick check
steps.prompt: Why is there no word for "is" in this sentence?

options.label: Arabic has no present-tense "is / are" — the two words sit side by side
It was left out to keep the sentence short
The word for "is" comes only in questions

steps.explanation: A nominal sentence joins a definite topic (الْكِتَابُ) and an indefinite comment (جَدِيدٌ) with no verb between them.

steps.title: Quick check

options.label: الْبَابُ — it has الـ and no tanwīn
بَابٌ — the tanwīn ـٌ marks it as definite

steps.explanation: الـ makes a noun definite and the tanwīn drops. بَابٌ, with tanwīn, is "a door".

steps.title: Well read
steps.message: You now know four building blocks of A1 Arabic: singular/dual/plural, definite vs. indefinite, the verbless sentence, and negation with لَيْسَ. Practise them in the Review view to keep them.
